title: Time Period of a Wave
description: Master the last wave measurement — time period — and see how it links to frequency.

content.value: The TIME PERIOD is the time taken to complete ONE full oscillation. It is measured in seconds. If a pendulum takes 2 seconds to swing there and back once, its time period is 2 seconds.
Time Period and Frequency Are Linked

Time period and frequency are opposites of each other. If something vibrates quickly (high frequency), each oscillation takes a very short time (small time period). If it vibrates slowly, each oscillation takes longer.

1                            1
frequency = ───────────      time period = ───────────
            time period                     frequency

Example: frequency 2 Hz  →  time period = 1/2 = 0.5 s
         time period 0.25 s → frequency = 1/0.25 = 4 Hz
Suppose an object makes 5 oscillations in one second. Its frequency is 5 Hz. Its time period is 1 ÷ 5 = 0.2 seconds — each single oscillation takes one-fifth of a second.
Remember: frequency = 1 ÷ time period. High frequency always means a small time period, and low frequency means a large time period.
Key Takeaway: The time period is the time for one complete oscillation (in seconds), and it is the reciprocal of frequency: frequency = 1 ÷ time period.
